correctness.rationale: The Gaussian conditional information and independent Poisson clean probability produce exactly j_i(t,lambda)=exp(-lambda*t)t^2/[(t+a_i)(t+h_i)]. The logarithmic derivative is strictly decreasing from +infinity to -lambda, yielding one finite global maximum. Same-signed sum/product rankings imply strict denominator dominance. Opposite rankings make the difference of stationary curves a quadratic with one positive root. Envelope differentiation gives d/dlambda log(F1/F2)=t2-t1 and hence one log-ratio maximum; small-hazard sum asymptotics and large-hazard product asymptotics prove a unique mode crossing after that maximum, with a strict duration jump. The checker independently replayed 29,265 finite diagnostic assertions, supplementing but not replacing the analytical proof. The assumptions, equality cases, and physical limits are explicit.

originality.rationale: The exact necessary-and-sufficient one-switch classification concerns two independently reoptimized exposure modes as a common cosmic-ray hazard changes. The relevant Fixsen et al. 2000 full text and Regan--Stockman 2001 six-page memo were materially inspected. Regan--Stockman give a general information-per-time optimization method and fixed-parameter mode comparisons, a strong nearby predecessor; their recorded results do not state or prove the all-hazard single-crossing theorem or its sum/product criterion and discontinuous optimal-duration jump. A general optimization recipe is not logically a proof that two optimized curves have at most one crossing. The inspected material and subject-specific indexed results yielded no stronger covering statement. Novelty remains provisional pending independent literature review.
residual_risks: Regan--Stockman 2001 is a very close prior optimization framework. A separate uninspected appendix or other technical note could already state the comparative all-hazard switch theorem.
Anderson--Gordon 2011 full text was not examined; its abstract concerns a different algorithmic question, but complete exclusion of related mode comparisons is unwarranted.
Historical literature search is not exhaustive and no independent novelty determination has been made; absence of an indexed hit is not proof of priority.
The physical readout-hazard model is idealized and explicitly excludes partial ramp salvage, saturation and mode-specific cosmic-ray susceptibility.

value.rationale: A genuine operational question is to choose between a fast/high-read-noise mode and a slow/low-read-noise mode under changing radiation hazard while reoptimizing each duration. The result classifies every positive mode pair into permanent dominance, exact equivalence, or one and only one radiation-dependent reversal. The sum/product criterion, two distinct tied durations, exact mean-hit-time boundary and adaptive-mixing bound provide an interpretable sharp benchmark rather than a recomputed optimum at arbitrary numeric parameter values. This has mathematical value as a complete global classification within an instrument-motivated model; it is explicitly not field-calibrated flight guidance.
